gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.description: Learn how to set up your integration and make your first API call.
gettingStarted.step1: Obtain your integration credentials from the Spalf dashboard.
gettingStarted.step2: Authenticate with Cognito to get an access token.
gettingStarted.step3: Include the token in your API requests.
gettingStarted.step4: Start making API calls to manage reservations.

webhookSetup.title: Setting Up Webhooks
webhookSetup.description: Configure webhooks to receive real-time updates.
webhookSetup.step1: Create a webhook endpoint in your system to receive notifications.
webhookSetup.step2: Use the Integration API to create a webhook configuration.
webhookSetup.step3: Subscribe to the events you want to receive.
webhookSetup.step4: Verify webhook signatures to ensure authenticity.

reservationSync.title: Syncing Reservations
reservationSync.description: Keep your system in sync with Spalf reservations.
reservationSync.step1: Set up webhooks for reservation events.
reservationSync.step2: Process incoming webhooks to update your local data.
reservationSync.step3: Use the API to fetch reservation details as needed.
reservationSync.step4: Handle conflicts and edge cases gracefully.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.subtitle: Receive real-time notifications for events in Spalf
webhooks.overviewDescription: Webhooks allow your application to receive real-time notifications when events occur in Spalf. Instead of polling the API, webhooks push data to your server as soon as events happen.
webhooks.eventsDescription: Subscribe to one or more of these events when creating a webhook configuration.

eventTypes.reservationCreated: Triggered when a new reservation is created.
eventTypes.reservationUpdated: Triggered when a reservation is updated.
eventTypes.reservationCancelled: Triggered when a reservation is cancelled.
eventTypes.clientCreated: Triggered when a new client is created.
eventTypes.clientUpdated: Triggered when a client is updated.

webhooks.payloadDescription: All webhook payloads follow a consistent structure with the event type, timestamp, spa ID, and event-specific data.
webhooks.securityDescription: All webhook requests include a signature header for verification.
webhooks.signatureDescription: The X-Spalf-Signature header contains an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the payload using your webhook secret.
webhooks.verifyingDescription: Always verify webhook signatures to ensure the request came from Spalf.
